summary: Northbridge AI: Console cost estimate drift after enabling batching on Dedicated (requests explain/attribution output)
description:
Issue summary
Northbridge AI reports that after enabling batching on their Dedicated deployment, Redwood Console’s cost estimate increased and no longer matches their observed/expected behavior. They are requesting SCM “explain” output so they can understand which factors changed (batch efficiency, prefill/decode split, cache assumptions, quant profile) and whether the estimate is using actual measured batch_size_effective vs configured max.

Customer impact
- Console Cost Breakdown page shows ~+12% to +20% higher estimated compute cost per 1M output tokens after batching was enabled.
- Customer expected batching to reduce cost; they are concerned this indicates regression/mis-accounting.
- No billing dispute yet; customer explicitly asked for “explain” output to validate assumptions before escalating internally.

Customer context / environment
- Customer: Northbridge AI (enterprise)
- Deployment: Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- Model: llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Quantization profile: qp-int8-per-channel-v3 (per customer notes; confirm via catalog lookup)
- Batching change (customer-provided): enabled continuous batching, max_batch_tokens=4096, max_concurrent_sequences=8; change rolled out 2025-02-08 ~21:00 UTC
- Console page impacted: Cost Breakdown > Route-level estimate

What the customer observed
- Before batching enabled: Console estimate roughly tracked their internal cost model (GPU-hour based), within ~5–7%.
- After batching enabled: Console estimate increased despite token throughput improving; they estimate actual GPU cost per token decreased.

Artifacts provided by customer (sanitized)
- Route: /v1/chat/completions (streaming)
- Typical request: input 2.5k–4k tokens, output 0.8k–1.5k tokens
- Example Redwood request IDs (customer pasted):
  - rwd_req_01HNBX3Z1Q9QY0WJY0Y7T4M2AQ
  - rwd_req_01HNBX6M7R2K8A3P0C1N5Q1W9D
- Time window: 2025-02-09 00:00–06:00 UTC

Initial hypothesis
Estimate path may be using configured batching parameters (or pre-admission counters) rather than post-admission batch_size_effective, producing incorrect batch efficiency factor in SCM compute attribution. This would present as drift specifically after enabling batching.

Request from customer
- Provide SCM explain output (breakdown + contributing factors + assumptions + confidence) for at least one request ID/time window.
- Confirm whether the cost estimate is “estimated” vs “metered attribution” and what signals are missing/assumed.

Notes
- SCM outputs are not the source of truth for invoices (per program scope). Customer is focused on Console transparency and internal validation.

2025-02-10 09:14 (Dylan Brooks, Support/Console)
Customer escalation from Northbridge AI CS channel. They say enabling batching should reduce unit cost but Console estimate increased ~15%. They’re asking for an “explain output” that shows what inputs SCM used (batch size, cache hit rate, prefill/decode split). Assigning to Felix (cost views) + tagging runtime/telemetry as needed.

2025-02-10 11:02 (Felix Schneider)
Ack. Likely in SCM compute component: batch_efficiency_factor derived from batch_size_effective. I’m pulling SCM logs for the time window and comparing estimate vs attribution fields. Also checking if their tenant is on SCM v1 explain endpoint build.
Action: request customer to confirm whether batching was enabled via Redwood policy vs client-side concurrency change (so we can look for the right flags).

2025-02-10 11:18 (Dylan Brooks)
Customer confirmed batching enabled via Redwood Dedicated config change (not client-side). They flipped from batching=off to batching=on, with max_concurrent_sequences=8, max_batch_tokens=4096. No other routing/model change. They can share 2–3 request IDs and time window (already in ticket).

2025-02-11 08:41 (Omar El-Sayed)
Runtime note: there was a known issue last week where batch_size_effective emitted pre-admission (before admission control). This can overstate effective batch size during spikes / queueing conditions. If SCM consumes that, estimate can look better/worse depending on which side uses it.
I think PR-18618 is the fix (“computed pre-admission control; adds regression tests”). Need to confirm rollout state for us-east Dedicated fleet.

2025-02-11 10:12 (Felix Schneider)
Confirmed in logs for tenant northbridge-ai: SCM compute component uses batch_size_effective from runtime signal batch_size_effective_v1. During the customer’s window, the value shows step change right after batching enabled, but distribution looks suspicious (p50=7.9, p95=8.0 almost constant) which doesn’t match their traffic profile.
This suggests we’re using the configured max / pre-admission signal rather than true effective batching.
Next: verify fleet version and whether the PR-18618 fix has rolled to Dedicated us-east.

2025-02-12 13:27 (Sean Gallagher)
SRE: Dedicated us-east is partially rolled on the runtime patch; ~60% pods updated as of 12:30 UTC. Full rollout expected by end of day barring canary failures. Suggest we wait for full rollout then re-check SCM estimate distribution for batch_size_effective.

2025-02-13 09:05 (Felix Schneider)
After rollout completion (per SRE), batch_size_effective distribution looks more realistic (p50 ~2.1, p95 ~5.8). Console estimate for the same route window drops ~13% relative to yesterday. This matches the customer’s expectation that batching reduces cost.
We should provide an SCM explain output sample (redacted) and a brief statement: estimate drift was due to incorrect batch_size_effective signal prior to runtime fix; now corrected.
Also: explain endpoint exists but returns customer-sensitive breakdown; ensure we only share within the customer’s own tenant context via support-approved process.

2025-02-13 10:22 (Dr. Aisha Rahman)
Security reminder: do not paste raw internal cost coefficients or cross-tenant SKU pricing details into customer emails. OK to share the customer’s own breakdown/assumptions/confidence and relative factors (e.g., “batch efficiency lower than assumed”). Any screenshots/payloads should be generated from their tenant context and redacted for internal-only fields.

2025-02-14 16:03 (Dylan Brooks)
Sent customer update: identified incorrect batching effectiveness input used in estimate during partial runtime rollout; fix rolled out to us-east Dedicated. Offered to provide explain output for their request IDs once they confirm which ones are representative post-fix.
Customer asked specifically: can explain show (1) batch efficiency factor, (2) prefill vs decode, (3) confidence/assumptions when telemetry missing.
I responded yes, and we’ll provide a sanitized excerpt.

2025-02-17 09:48 (Felix Schneider)
Generated explain output excerpt for request rwd_req_01HNBX6M7R2K8A3P0C1N5Q1W9D (post-fix). Summary:
- Total estimated technical cost decreased vs pre-fix by ~14%.
- Largest driver: compute component adjusted by observed batch_efficiency (effective batch size lower than configured max).
- Assumptions listed: cache state assumed “warm=false” due to missing kv_cache_warmth tag for this route; confidence marked “medium”.
- Contributing factors: prefill/decode split, quant profile id, region.
Shared with Support as customer-safe paragraph; keeping full JSON payload internal.
Next: follow-up task for telemetry to ensure kv_cache_warmth tag present for Dedicated routes to improve confidence.

2025-02-18 14:20 (Dylan Brooks)
Customer confirmed the updated Console estimate now aligns with their observed GPU-hour accounting within ~6–8%. They’re satisfied with the explanation and asked us to improve confidence messaging when cache tags are missing.
Marking Resolved. Follow-up noted for telemetry tagging consistency (not tracked here; to be filed separately if needed).
resolution:
Root cause: batch_size_effective signal was computed/emitted pre-admission control in part of the runtime fleet, causing SCM to apply an incorrect batch efficiency factor after batching was enabled. This led to estimate drift (Console) for Northbridge AI.

Fix: Runtime patch (redwood/pr-18618) rolled out to Dedicated us-east fleet; SCM explain endpoint (redwood/pr-18677) used to produce attribution/explain excerpt confirming corrected factors.

Customer outcome: Console estimate returned to expected range; customer received sanitized explanation of major drivers (batch efficiency + prefill/decode split) and confidence/assumptions.

Notes: No billing changes; SCM outputs remain for transparency/optimization only. Telemetry follow-up suggested for missing cache-warmth tagging to improve confidence.
